headline: Strong bar and worship ratings sit alongside a shortfall in park space in Ward 36.
summary:
Belmont Cragin, West Town, Montclare, and Humboldt Park make up Ward 36, on Chicago's Northwest Side. The ward sits 27th among the city's 50 wards, scoring 45.79 out of 100. Two of its top scores trace back to city government activity. It leads every ward in Chicago on bills sponsored, a count of non-routine legislation tied to this council session, and it also tops the city on the cut of infrastructure menu money spent on alley repair. Its houses of worship post some of the highest ratings anywhere in Chicago, and its bars score among the best in the city.

The softer numbers cluster around green space, health access, and street friction. Park acreage per resident sits well below most of the city, mental health providers per resident are scarce next to most wards, and parking complaints run higher here than almost anywhere in Chicago. Demolition permits and mapped landmarks also land in the bottom ten. Put together, this is a dense stretch of the city with strong food, drink, and worship options, next to real gaps in park space and mental health access.
reading_the_rankings: Ward 36's top spot on bills sponsored carries an asterisk. Chicago redrew ward boundaries in 2023, so the count reflects today's district lines more than one alderman's full term in the seat, and the underlying data only carries a medium-confidence label. Fifth place on the city's traffic proximity index tells a similar story from a different angle. That figure gets assigned by area from census tracts rather than measured block by block, so some of what shows up here really belongs to the wards next door, and the rank also reads sharper than it is, since fourteen other wards land inside two points of this one. Forty-fifth for mental health providers per resident looks worse than the real gap behind it. Only two points separate Ward 36 from twenty-five other wards on this measure, and the typical spread across the middle of the city here runs to just seven points, so most wards, whatever their overall rank, look a lot alike on this one.

news.headline: Ukrainian Village, Bucktown Apartment Proposals Approved By City Council
news.note: City Council approved a 40-unit apartment building at Chicago and Washtenaw avenues on the Ukrainian Village-Humboldt Park border, part of Ward 36, after two rounds of community meetings over the project's size.

news.headline: With Airbag Thefts Still Up, Could A New Ordinance Curb The Black Market Sales Fueling Them?
news.note: An ordinance backed by Ald. Gilbert Villegas targets auto shops that resell stolen airbags, responding to a rise in thefts across the Northwest Side, including parts of Ward 36.

news.headline: City Council committee backs crackdown on selling weed near schools, parks
news.note: A City Council committee advanced an ordinance from Ward 36's Ald. Gilbert Villegas penalizing marijuana sales near schools and parks, after a scaled back compromise on the restricted zone.
